headline: High-risk shared-workspace automation: n8n can overwrite or act on aci outputs, creating dangerous prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-action paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest and emit CRM/email/research content, while n8n can read/write server files and orchestrate tools via workflow nodes. That creates a plausible shared-channel pathway where attacker-controlled content from aci can be fed into n8n workflows and treated as instructions. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF aci output is copied into an n8n workflow input or file
IF n8n parses that content as instructions or node parameters
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter and schema check before n8n consumes aci output
Disable automatic execution of any workflow step fed by aci text
Review one representative workflow for prompt-injection handling
Log and alert on unexpected node-parameter changes
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between aci and n8n

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; n8n reads and writes the server filesystem and can send workflow data through many integrations. If aci outputs sensitive records into n8n, n8n can persist or forward them beyond the original context, creating a realistic leakage path in default use. The blast radius includes multiple data classes and external services.
conditions: IF aci passes CRM or email content into an n8n workflow
IF that workflow writes files or sends data to an external integration node
mitigations: Restrict n8n workflows to a minimal allowlist of integrations
Mask or redact CRM/email fields before handoff
Store aci outputs in a short-lived temp directory only
Audit one workflow for unintended file persistence
requires-engineering: enforce field-level data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad network egress, while n8n supports server filesystem writes, shell execution, subprocesses, and shared state via datastore/connected systems. If both operate on the same workspace or downstream systems, concurrent writes and side effects can collide without locking. The overlap is enough for destructive race conditions and inconsistent state.
conditions: IF aci and n8n target the same files, credentials, or external records
IF n8n workflows run concurrently with aci actions
mitigations: Separate aci and n8n into distinct workspaces
Disable concurrent runs for shared resources
Add file- and record-level locks around shared outputs
Check one workflow for overlapping write targets
requires-engineering: introduce transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/research outputs, and n8n is explicitly an orchestrator that can execute downstream nodes and commands. If n8n treats aci output as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated aci result can cascade into emails, file writes, or other actions without verification. That is a default-dangerous action chain with potentially irreversible effects.
conditions: IF n8n uses aci output as a trigger or parameter source
IF downstream nodes send messages, modify records, or execute commands
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before action nodes
Require structured validation of aci outputs
Limit downstream nodes to read-only actions during testing
Inspect one workflow for direct output-to-action wiring
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, calendar, and support data, while n8n processes whatever the workflow touches and stores credentials on its server. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated customer data is routed into n8n workflows with different retention or residency controls. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from aci enters an n8n workflow
IF n8n retention, logging, or residency settings differ from the source system
mitigations: Review retention settings for one n8n workflow
Exclude regulated fields from workflow payloads
Document the data-class mapping for aci-to-n8n transfers
Check credential storage scope on the n8n server
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
